outcome: Help teams review captions, audio description, age classification, sensitive content, brand rules and distribution requirements before release.
overview: Release volume has outgrown the compliance desk: captions, audio description, age classification, sensitive-content flags, brand rules and per-platform delivery requirements all have to be checked before publication, and inconsistent metadata means defects surface after release. This solution reviews programmes and advertisements against versioned regional policy, measures caption accuracy, timing and reading rate, drafts audio description for a human to refine, and flags age and brand concerns with time codes so a reviewer can jump straight to the moment. Nothing publishes without a named approval. A 6–12 week pilot targets shorter review cycles and fewer escaped defects, with accessibility experts and standards reviewers deciding.

benefits.text: Reduce compliance review time per asset by concentrating reviewer attention on time-coded flags rather than full watch-throughs
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Validated against the standards desk’s own review baseline during the pilot; complex or culturally sensitive material still needs full review — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce accessibility and brand defects escaping to release through automated pre-publication checks
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Automated checks catch measurable defects such as caption timing, reading rate and missing description; they do not judge cultural appropriateness or editorial intent

benefits.text: Record a named human approval and a correction trail for every released asset, with a working rollback
benefits.source: Workflow design — the publish gate blocks release without a named reviewer decision
benefits.limits: Applies to assets released through the governed workflow; direct-publish channels remain outside it

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); assets, policy versions, review decisions and complaint records remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: There is no written accessibility, age-classification or brand policy to evaluate against
notFor.why: Every check is an evaluation against a versioned policy; without one the system would impose an implicit, unaccountable standard of its own

notFor.situation: Automated blocking or classification without expert review is the goal
notFor.why: Classification carries cultural judgement and real consequences for what audiences may see; over-blocking is a censorship risk and under-blocking a safety risk, so a trained reviewer decides

notFor.situation: Trained accessibility and standards reviewers are not available
notFor.why: Draft audio description and caption assessments require expert refinement; without reviewers the pilot produces unreviewed output rather than compliant releases

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns accessibility, age and brand policy and every release, override and appeal decision · Duration: 6–12 week pilot; further 14–26 weeks to multi-market rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, media-analysis engineer, accessibility engineer; customer standards owner, accessibility specialist, child-safety reviewer, brand compliance lead · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and review baseline agreement
2) Policy versioning and regional rule encoding
3) Analysis, description and reviewer-workspace build
4) Bilingual expert evaluation and calibration
5) Publish-gate, rollback and complaint-path testing with UAT
6) Stabilisation and handover

Standards UAT complete, including user testing with the affected audience for audio description
